summary: This Wikipedia-derived note gives an overview of Namibia, a southern African country that gained independence from South Africa in 1990. It covers the country's geography and climate, especially its dryness and reliance on groundwater, along with its languages, colonial history, and the independence process. It also describes the economy, unemployment, education, tourism, and the make-up of the population.
one_line: Overview of Namibia's geography, colonial and independence history, languages, economy, tourism, and population.
key_facts: Namibia gained independence from South Africa on 21 March 1990, following the Namibian War of Independence.
Windhoek is the capital and largest city of Namibia.
Namibia borders Zambia and Angola to the north, Botswana to the east, South Africa to the south and east, and the Atlantic Ocean to the west.
Namibia is the driest country in sub-Saharan Africa and depends largely on groundwater.
With an average rainfall of about 350 mm per annum, the highest rainfall occurs in the Caprivi in the northeast (about 600 mm per annum).
Up to 1990, English, German and Afrikaans were official languages; SWAPO then instituted English as the sole official language, though only about 3% of the population speaks it as a home language.
The Portuguese navigators Diogo Cão in 1485 and Bartolomeu Dias in 1486 were the first Europeans to disembark and explore the region.
South West Africa became known as Namibia by the UN when the General Assembly changed the territory's name by Resolution 2372 (XXII) of 12 June 1968.
Namibia became the 160th member of the UN on 23 April 1990.
A combined UN civilian and peace-keeping force called UNTAG, under Finnish diplomat Martti Ahtisaari, was deployed from April 1989 to March 1990.
The South African-backed Democratic Turnhalle Alliance (DTA) became the official opposition after the November 1989 elections, which SWAPO won without the two-thirds majority it had hoped for.
The country's unemployment rate is 27.4% according to the Namibia Labour Force Survey Report 2012, conducted by the Namibia Statistics Agency.
In 1998, there were 400,325 Namibian students in primary school and 115,237 students in secondary schools.
In 2013, Bloomberg named Namibia the top emerging market economy in Africa and the 13th best in the world.
According to The Namibia Tourism Exit Survey, 56% of all tourists visiting Namibia during 2012-2013 visited Windhoek.

entities.name: Namibia
entities.role: Southern African country that is the subject of the note; its independence from South Africa came in 1990.

entities.name: Windhoek
entities.role: Capital and largest city of Namibia, central to its tourism and home to many tourism bodies.

entities.name: South Africa
entities.role: Neighbouring country that occupied and administered Namibia (then South-West Africa) and later withdrew under a 1988 agreement.

entities.name: SWAPO
entities.role: Political party that opposed South African rule and chose English as Namibia's sole official language.

entities.name: UNTAG
entities.role: United Nations Transition Assistance Group, a combined civilian and peace-keeping force that monitored the peace process and elections.

entities.name: Martti Ahtisaari
entities.role: Finnish diplomat under whom UNTAG was deployed.

entities.name: Diogo Cão
entities.role: Portuguese navigator who was among the first Europeans to disembark and explore the region in 1485.

entities.name: Bartolomeu Dias
entities.role: Portuguese navigator who was among the first Europeans to disembark and explore the region in 1486.

entities.name: Democratic Turnhalle Alliance
entities.role: South African-backed party that became the official opposition after the November 1989 elections.

entities.name: Namibian War of Independence
entities.role: Conflict that preceded Namibia's independence from South Africa on 21 March 1990.

entities.name: Namibia Tourism Board
entities.role: Primary tourism governing body, established by the Namibia Tourism Board Act, 2000, to regulate the tourism industry and market Namibia.

entities.name: Bloomberg
entities.role: Global business and financial news provider that named Namibia the top emerging market economy in Africa in 2013.

entities.name: Namibia Statistics Agency
entities.role: Body that conducted the Namibia Labour Force Survey Report 2012.
